rules.text: mini proves a useful agent is ~100 lines: bash-only tools, linear history, subprocess.run per action. When we add agent capability, build the smallest loop first — scaffold complexity is where bugs and drift live.

Third-party LLM keys stay forbidden. The llm-bridge (port 3048) exposes an OpenAI-compatible endpoint over our own z-ai backend; any OpenAI/litellm client runs against sovereign infrastructure. This also re-opens the reef-infra activation route blocked in r162.

Native tool-calling scaffolds assume tool_calls in responses. For models served as plain text through the bridge, use mini's LitellmTextbasedModel + mini_textbased.yaml (```mswea_bash_command format) — measured: 5/5 correct actions incl. Hebrew file content.

Unknown-model cost tracking is disabled (MSWEA_COST_TRACKING=ignore_errors) because our bridge reports estimated tokens (chars/4). Any real spend accounting must come from fleet-side counters, never invented prices.
Agents are fleet services too: llm-bridge is declared in fleet.yaml (FLO-1). Every new agent loop gets a manifest row before its second run.

activationRoutes.condition: a recurring fleet chore needs reasoning over files (repo hygiene, digest drafting, triage)
activationRoutes.action: run mini with a task file against llm-bridge, bounded by step_limit, in a scratch cwd; commit outputs through the normal evidence flow

whyNotRevenue: mini-swe-agent itself earns nothing; it is a capability unlock: sovereign autonomous coding/ops agent with zero marginal API cost. Indirect value: fleet chores that needed human-grade reasoning can now run bounded and local.
